title: Work in the Age of Machines
text:
Automation is reshaping the labour market faster than most governments anticipated. Routine tasks in manufacturing and administration are increasingly performed by software and robots, which has prompted fears of widespread unemployment. Economists, however, remain divided on whether technology will eliminate jobs or simply transform them. Historically, each wave of innovation has created new occupations that nobody could have foreseen.

The more pressing challenge, many analysts argue, is not the number of jobs but the skills required to perform them. Workers who can adapt through continuous retraining are likely to fare far better than those who rely on a single set of competencies. Consequently, several companies have begun investing heavily in internal learning programmes. Whether these initiatives will reach the workers who need them most remains an open question.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what has prompted fears of widespread unemployment?
options: Routine tasks being performed by software and robots
Workers refusing to retrain for new roles
Economists agreeing on a single forecast

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do many analysts consider the more pressing challenge?
options: Building new universities for technology students
The skills required to perform jobs

questions.text: What can be inferred about the effect of past waves of innovation on employment?
options: They have consistently destroyed more jobs than they created
They have tended to create occupations that were previously unimaginable
They have never affected administrative work
They have had no effect on the labour market

questions.text: What does the author suggest about corporate learning programmes?
options: They are guaranteed to benefit every employee
They may not necessarily reach the workers who need them most
They are being cancelled because of low demand
They are offered only to senior executives

vocabulary.definition: changing the form or structure of something
teaching workers new skills so they can do different jobs
as a result of something that has happened

paragraph_translations: A automação está remodelando o mercado de trabalho mais rapidamente do que a maioria dos governos previa. Tarefas rotineiras na manufatura e na administração são cada vez mais executadas por softwares e robôs, o que despertou temores de desemprego generalizado. Os economistas, no entanto, continuam divididos quanto a saber se a tecnologia eliminará empregos ou apenas os transformará. Historicamente, cada onda de inovação criou novas ocupações que ninguém poderia ter previsto.

O desafio mais urgente, argumentam muitos analistas, não é o número de empregos, mas as habilidades necessárias para exercê-los. Trabalhadores que conseguem se adaptar por meio de requalificação contínua tendem a se sair muito melhor do que aqueles que dependem de um único conjunto de competências. Consequentemente, várias empresas começaram a investir fortemente em programas internos de aprendizagem. Se essas iniciativas chegarão aos trabalhadores que mais precisam delas continua sendo uma questão em aberto.
